title: Adapter coverage parity: crash-and-resume verification tests for the LangGraph and OpenAI Agents adapters (Cyrax321/CONTINUUM)
raw_text:
Adapter coverage parity: crash-and-resume verification tests for the LangGraph and OpenAI Agents adapters — open-source issue in Cyrax321/CONTINUUM. Labels: help wanted, adapter. ## Affected component

Adapters (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents, LangChain, generic)

## What problem does this solve?

README's Status section states it directly: the OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph adapters do not yet carry the same crash-and-resume verification coverage as the generic facade. That makes it hard to recommend them for production recovery, and it is exactly the kind of gap an external contributor with framework experience can close.

## Proposed solution

Port the crash-and-resume ver
summary: This open-source issue focuses on improving the reliability of ai agent frameworks like langgraph and openai agents by adding "crash-and-resume verification tests." in essence, these tests ensure that if an ai application or agent encounters an unexpected error and crashes, it can gracefully recover and resume its operation from where it left off, rather than losing all progress. this is a critical aspect of building robust and production-ready ai systems, especially for long-running or complex agent workflows. contributing to such a task would deepen your understanding of software engineering best practices for ai, fault tolerance, and the intricacies of agent frameworks. you could investigate how state management is handled in these frameworks to enable such recovery.
why: Focuses on building robust, fault-tolerant AI agents, crucial for production MLOps.

title: RAG with LangChain for Beginners 🚀 | Hugging Face + ChromaDB + Free LLM in Google Colab | Tutorial
author: Cloudsoft Solutions
raw_text: Want to learn **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) from scratch?** In this beginner-friendly tutorial, we build a **complete ...
summary: this youtube tutorial offers a beginner-friendly introduction to building a complete retrieval-augmented generation (rag) system from scratch. it guides you through using popular tools like langchain for orchestration, hugging face models for the language model component, and chromadb as a vector database. the entire setup is designed to be runnable in google colab, making it highly accessible without needing powerful local hardware. understanding rag is crucial for making llms more accurate and up-to-date by providing them with external, relevant information. you could follow this tutorial to build your very first end-to-end rag application and see how these components work together.
why: hands-on rag tutorial using popular tools, essential for practical llm applications.
